The proposed detector (non-USD principal unit whose printed row lacks that currency code) is concrete and uses data the bridge already holds; false positives limited to rows with no printed par (the report names one, Speed Midco undrawn '-'), which the check should skip.

Section-total-by-class comparison is concrete and recurrence-catching; false positives only where a filer's section totals mix classes, which the comparison would surface rather than hide.

trza flagged 11 issuer_name_printed rows (8 digit/v plus 3 Coding Solution), trzd 0. issuer_name_printed is the right existing detector: it compares against the printed company cell, so glued digits recur-detect at any fund. Fixing by row correction keeps the default ' n' number strip intact (see next observation).

Measured trzb page_rule_findings: 3,314 issuer_name_printed rows for this fund (13 fund-quarter findings) against 11 in trza, so the wrapper setting broke nearly every name, a larger effect than the report's '5 to 13' wording suggests. Reverting was correct. existing_detector holds: issuer_name_printed fired on every damaged row, so a recurrence cannot pass silently. Mechanism not identified by the investigator; pipeline/issuer_instrument_split.py says the shared default deliberately does not cut row numbers and leaves that to the wrapper's issuer_name_strip_re, so a strip_re that does not itself remove ' n' leaves numbers in place.

Leaving it as an observation is right if a correction on a derived field is not applied; field diff trze vs trzd is empty, consistent with the removed correction. The proposed fix (round the derived cash leg) is a shared-code proposal, concrete and with negligible false-positive risk.
